headline: Chips Carry Momentum Into Wednesday as Oil and Iran Diplomacy Set the Tone
body_html:
Wall Street approaches Wednesday's open with oil back in focus and semiconductors coming off a standout session. Crude was reported more than 1% higher after Yemen's Houthis claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, reviving supply worries. Meanwhile, Qatari mediators have put a new proposal to Iran aimed at ending the war.

Tuesday's completed session left a constructive backdrop. In our 540-stock universe, 322 stocks rose and 215 fell. Semiconductors led the sectors with a 4.39% advance, powered by MaxLinear (up 12.34%), Alpha and Omega Semiconductor (up 11.52%) and Credo Technology (up 10.77%). Materials gained 2.12% and industrials 1.11%, while software slipped 0.61% and consumer names 0.26%.

Moves under the surface were sharp. Xylem fell 14.21% and Valero Energy 9.24%, even as the energy group edged up 0.24%. Pentair jumped 12.80%. At the open, watch whether chip leadership holds, how crude reacts to Saudi headlines, and whether easing AI debt worries survive ahead of updates from Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon. Early prices are thin and should be treated with caution.

briefs.headline: Refinery Strike Claim Revives Supply Worries
briefs.body: Crude oil was reported up more than 1% after the Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery with a missile. The claim has refocused traders on Gulf supply risk. Energy stocks gained only 0.24% on Tuesday, so the group enters the open with room to react.

briefs.headline: Qatar Brings Iran a New Proposal to End the War
briefs.body: Mediators from Qatar have presented Iran with a fresh plan aimed at ending the conflict, an official said. Any sign of movement could shift sentiment in oil and defence-sensitive shares. Markets will watch for Tehran's response and for how quickly the diplomacy progresses.

briefs.headline: Standard Chartered Surges After Raising Its Outlook
briefs.body: Shares of Standard Chartered jumped after the bank lifted its full-year targets and reported profit well above analyst forecasts. The strong result gives global banks a positive early-session reference. Investors will look to see whether the optimism spreads to other lenders.

briefs.headline: Robinhood Revenue Climbs 12% Despite Crypto Slump
briefs.body: Robinhood reported quarterly revenue up 12%, with event contracts and options trading making up for weakness in crypto. The mix shows retail activity moving toward derivatives-style products. Expect attention on the stock at the open as investors judge how durable that shift is.

briefs.headline: AI Debt Anxiety Eases Before Big Tech Updates
briefs.body: Worries about financing for artificial-intelligence spending have cooled ahead of reports from Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon. Tuesday's 4.39% semiconductor gain shows how much sentiment matters. Software, down 0.61%, lagged, so those updates may decide whether the chip rally broadens.

briefs.headline: UK Budget Expected to Be Low-Key, Cash ISA Cuts Reversed
briefs.body: Britain's chancellor, Healey, is aiming for a restrained budget as the country faces what he calls a difficult moment. The Financial Times reports he will reverse planned cuts to cash ISA allowances. Sterling and gilt traders will watch for any surprises beyond that.
